name: ONE Gas
headline: The regulated natural gas distributor for most of Oklahoma and Kansas and part of Texas.
what_short: Regulated natural gas utility (Oklahoma, Kansas, Texas)
what_it_does: ONE Gas delivers natural gas through buried pipe networks to homes and businesses. It serves about 89% of gas-distribution customers in Oklahoma, 72% in Kansas and 13% in Texas. State regulators set the rates it may charge.
why_it_passed: It holds the gas-distribution franchise in its areas, and a rival would have to duplicate the whole buried pipe network street by street.
Regulators allow it set returns on equity: 9.40% in Oklahoma, 9.60% in Kansas and 9.80% in Texas.
It earned 7.5% to 9.0% a year on its book equity across 2016 to 2025, a steady regulated return.
Spending above depreciation, about $690 million a year against $246 million, grows the base on which regulators let it earn a return.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what this utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At $78.36 a share the price is above the analysis's value range of $66.59 to $68.70, and the expected return is only about 4.7% a year, against 5.31% on a 30-year US Treasury bond.
watch: Debt was about $3.4 billion in mid-2026, and $771 million of commercial paper must be rolled over within 270 days.
Winter Storm Uri in February 2021 forced it to find about $2 billion for gas costs and raise $2.5 billion in new notes.
All its business is in three adjoining states, and an event such as a major pipeline accident could hurt a single utility badly.
